answer: Two agents cross-sign a proof-of-personhood claim. The claim stays in escrow until finality. A rotating auditor pool re-checks both signatures, and an identity whose escrow never clears cannot vote or earn. Edge case: if a signer drops before finality the claim reverts and both parties lose the epoch. A farm then needs two live, unrelated islands per account, doubling the harbor of keys it must keep funded and answering to reach the zenith of a payout.
